summary: Manhattan Beach sits on just over three square miles of actual land — much of its ten-square-mile official boundary is open ocean — yet packs a median home price that exceeds $2 million, yielding a price-to-income ratio above 10:1 even against a median household income of nearly $194,000. That ratio is the defining tension of daily life here: the income floor is already remarkably high, and housing still dwarfs it. The city occupies a gentle coastal slope between the Strand bike path along the Pacific and the low hills east of Sepulveda Boulevard, giving much of the western half direct ocean breezes and sunset views from rooftop decks. The aerospace and defense corridor along El Segundo Boulevard sits minutes north, and a cluster of corporate offices — including Skechers' global headquarters — means some residents commute measured in single-digit minutes rather than freeway hours. An average of 9.1 hours of daily sunshine and a year-round high near 73°F make the beach itself a persistent, practical amenity rather than a weekend novelty. Downtown's walkable blocks along Manhattan Beach Boulevard run from Highland Avenue down to the pier, concentrating restaurants, coffee shops, and boutiques into a compact stretch that generates real pedestrian activity most evenings. Manhattan Beach is essentially a small coastal city with big-metro incomes layered on top of small-town square footage — a place where the ocean is never more than a short walk away, but the price of that proximity is never abstract.
